A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same noise-space domain adaptation work. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained, relocated, and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original denoising, deraining, and deblurring experiments, component ablations, architecture-scaling results, and additional qualitative evaluations in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds conditioning ablations, deeper-backbone results, and further comparative and qualitative evidence.

M1.justification: The diffusion adaptation objective, joint training, channel shuffling, residual-swapping loss, inference procedure, and unpaired-clean-image extension remain unchanged. Ours* tests the existing strategy with a deeper U-Net; it does not introduce a new adaptation component.

E1.justification: Training datasets and the SIDD, SPA, and RealBlur-J evaluation tasks remain unchanged. DND and Real-Internet evaluations already appear in v1's appendix; their appearance in v2's main text and revised example selections do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 5 adds SIDD comparisons against C2N and AP-BSN, while Table A2 introduces a complexity comparison with several restoration methods. Comparator membership in Tables 1–3 is unchanged. PUCA is newly cited but has no reported comparison results.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluations using the deeper Ours* backbone and synthetic-only or real-only conditioning controls. Table 5 also identifies the asymmetric pixel-shuffle setting for AP-BSN. The existing experiments retain their datasets, metrics, patch size, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, and diffusion schedule.

E4.justification: Table 4 adds controls examining the contribution of synthetic and real conditioning inputs, extending v1's noise-range and shortcut-prevention ablations. Section 4.3 and Appendix A4.2 add deeper-backbone texture comparisons and cross-method complexity analysis. The original scaling study and unpaired-extension analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, variability estimates, or significance tests for the restoration comparisons. v2 continues the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3, existing ablation rows, scaling-plot values, and the relocated unpaired-extension results are unchanged. New PSNR/SSIM entries include synthetic-only 26.83/0.6286, real-only 32.60/0.8831, and Ours* 35.52/0.9297. Table 5 adds C2N at 35.35/0.9370 and AP-BSN at 34.90/0.9000; C2N exceeds Ours* in SSIM. These are added comparisons and model configurations, not improvements under the original model setting. Complexity results and some qualitative examples are also added or replaced.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 replaces distribution notation with explicit random-variable notation and a distribution-equality goal, restating the existing alignment objective. Equations 1–5 remain mathematically equivalent. Neither version supplies formal guarantees or proofs, and v2 adds none.

C1.justification: The central novelty claim—noise-space adaptation through a training-only diffusion model—is retained. v2 explicitly claims independence from prior noise/degradation knowledge in its contribution list and adds a conclusion claiming scalability beyond self-supervised methods across restoration tasks.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 replaces v1's discussion of retraining for new domains/tasks and potential proxy-model reuse with an explanation of weaker sensitivity to blur and low-frequency degradation. The earlier broader-impact discussion, including possible alteration of original information, disappears. Appendix A3 adds distinct explanations for real conditions supplying corrective gradients and synthetic conditions guiding early training; Section 4.3 also qualifies performance through backbone capacity.

D1.justification: v2 adds parameter and GMAC information for Ours* and comparison methods, although Ours*'s exact layer configuration remains unspecified. Existing backbone configurations and most hyperparameters are retained. The NVIDIA A100 disclosure is removed, and the promised GitHub code-release link is replaced by a project-page link; the PDF does not establish that code was released.

R1.justification: v2 adds C2N, AP-BSN, PUCA, and recent diffusion-adaptation references by Welker, Gou, and Daultani and colleagues. It distinguishes its training-only diffusion proxy from methods requiring diffusion during inference and expands its comparison with self-supervised learning. The original feature-space/pixel-space/noise-space positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are edited, contributions become explicit bullets, and the scalability discussion gains subheadings and explanatory prose. The unpaired-extension discussion moves from Section 4.1 to Appendix A4.1, and appendix sections are regrouped. The overall section sequence and much of the methodological narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 removes v1's separate framework Figure 2, annotates Figure 1 with gradient guidance, adds Tables 5 and A2 and texture-comparison Figure A2, and assembles earlier appendix examples into main-text Figure 8. Several qualitative panels are replaced or redistributed, and v1 Table 4 moves to Table A1. These changes accompany document-wide header, typography, table-highlighting, and layout revisions.

improvement.justification: The added C2N/AP-BSN comparisons, backbone accuracy/complexity results, and conditioning ablations modestly strengthen the empirical assessment, while the blur limitation clarifies applicability. The gains are constrained: Ours* is incompletely specified, the conditioning ablations also differ in CS/RS settings, and earlier retraining and hardware disclosures are lost. Overall, v2 provides useful additional context and evidence without substantially resolving the paper's remaining evidential limitations.
